papers.title: Fixation Release and the Bone Bandaid: A New Bone Fixation Device Paradigm.
papers.abstract: The current gold standard of care for mandibular segmental defeat reconstruction is the use of Ti-6Al-4V immobilization hardware and fibular double barrel graft. This method is often successful immediately at restoring mandible function, however the highly stiff fixation hardware causes stress shielding of the grafted bone and stress concentration in the fixation device over time which can lead to fixation device failure and revision surgery. The purpose of reconstructive surgery could be to create normal stress trajectories in the mandible following engraftment. We investigate the use of a two stage mechanism which separates the immobilization/healing and regenerative phases of mandibular segmental defect treatment. The device includes the use of a very stiff, Ti-6Al-4V, releasable mechanism which assures bone healing. Therefore it could be released once the reconstructed boney tissue and any of its ligamentous attachments have completely healed. Underneath the released Ti-6Al-4V plate would be a pre-loaded nitinol (NiTi) wire-frame apparatus that facilitates the normal stress-strain trajectory through the engrafted bone after the graft is healed in place and the Ti-6Al-4V fixation device has been released. Due to the use of NiTi wires forming a netting that connects vascularized bone and possibly bone chips, bone grafts are also more likely to be incorporate rather than to resorb. We first evaluated a healthy adult mandible during normal mastication to obtain the normal stress-strain distribution. Then, we developed the finite element (FE) model of the mandibular reconstruction (in the M1-3 region) with the proposed fixation device during the healing (locked state) and post-healing (released state) periods. To recreate normal stress trajectory in the reconstructed mandible, we applied the Response Surface Methodology (RMS) to optimize the Bone Bandaid geometry (i.e., wire diameters and location). The results demonstrate that the proposed mechanism immobilizes the grafted bone in the locked state properly since the maximum resultant gap (21.54 micron) between the graft and host mandible surfaces are in the safe region (less than 300 micron). By considering the von Mises criteria for failure, FE analysis together with experimental studies (i.e., compressive and tensile testing on the inferior and superior fixation devices, respectively) confirm that the proposed fixation devices do not fail, showing safety factor of at least 10.3. Based on the Response Surface Methodology (RSM) technique, the optimal parameter values for the wires are achieved (0.65 mm and 1 mm for the superior and inferior wires, respectively) and the required level of preload on each wire are calculated (369.8 N and 229 N for the inferior and superior wires, respectively). The FE results for stress distribution on the reconstructed mandible during the released state closely match that of a healthy mandible.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究下颌骨重建，而非髋关节植入物或股骨柄，与用户方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper focuses on mandibular reconstruction, not hip implant or femoral stem; it does not quantify proximal femur stress shielding, micromotion, or contact mechanics in the hip joint.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决下颌骨重建中固定支架应力遮挡导致的骨吸收和修复失败问题。
summary_zh.method: 提出可释放Ti-6Al-4V板结合预载NiTi丝网的两阶段固定机构，并通过有限元和响应面法优化几何参数。
summary_zh.result: 释放后重建下颌骨的应力分布与健康下颌骨高度一致，固定状态最大间隙小于300微米，安全因子大于10.3。
summary_zh.validation: 通过压缩和拉伸实验验证固定装置的力学性能，并结合有限元结果评估。

summary_en.motivation: To prevent stress shielding and fixation failure in mandibular segmental defect reconstruction by introducing a two-stage fixation device that mimics normal bone stress trajectories.
summary_en.method: A releasable Ti-6Al-4V plate combined with a pre-loaded NiTi wire frame was designed; finite element analysis and response surface methodology optimized wire diameters and preloads.
summary_en.result: The released device restored physiological stress distribution in the reconstructed mandible, with a maximum gap of 21.54 μm (safe under 300 μm) and a safety factor of at least 10.3.
summary_en.validation: Experimental compressive and tensile tests validated the mechanical integrity of the fixation device, complemented by finite element simulations of the mandibular model.

papers.title: Developing Active Learning Tendency Scale for Academicians
papers.abstract: The purposeof this study was to develop the active learning tendency scale foracademicians. In this study, general survey method which is one of the methodsthat are often used especially to describe a situation to be searched withwider groups, was applied in the research. The study was conducted withacademicians in 2016-2017 academic years, autumn semester. The population ofthe research was Niğde University academicians. 126 academicians, who wereselected according to purposive sampling method, took part in the study. Asresult of the analyzing data, active learning tendencı scale for academicians whichhad 18 items contained one factor and these factors explained %40.17 of totalvariance were developed.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文与用户研究方向完全无关，属于教育学领域。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is about educational psychology scale development, with no connection to FEA, surrogate modeling, uncertainty quantification, or biomechanics.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发针对学术人员的主动学习倾向量表。
summary_zh.method: 采用一般调查法，对126名学术人员进行问卷调查和因子分析。
summary_zh.result: 开发出包含18个条目、单因子的主动学习倾向量表，解释总方差40.17%。
summary_zh.validation: 通过因子分析和信度检验进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a valid and reliable scale measuring academicians' tendency towards active learning.
summary_en.method: A general survey method was employed with 126 academicians selected via purposive sampling, followed by exploratory factor analysis.
summary_en.result: An 18-item, single-factor active learning tendency scale was developed, explaining 40.17% of the total variance.
summary_en.validation: The scale was validated through factor analysis and reliability analysis.
